question: Peat coal has ______ carbon and ______ moisture content?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Peat coal is a type of coal that is formed from partially decomposed vegetation.**
 
• It has a high moisture content and low **carbon content compared to other types of coal**.
 
• Typically, peat coal contains around **60-70%** water and has a carbon content ranging from **40-60%**.
 
• However, the exact carbon and moisture content can vary depending on the specific source and conditions of formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal is a combustible black or brownish-black sedimentary rock that is primarily composed of carbon, along with various other elements such as hydrogen, sulfur, oxygen, and nitrogen.**
 
• It is formed over millions of years from the remains of dead plants that have been subjected to high pressure and heat.
 
• **Coal is a fossil fuel**, and it is primarily used for energy production.
 
• It is burned to **produce heat,** which is then used to generate electricity or power industrial processes.
 
• **Coal** is also used in the production of **steel, cement, and other industrial materials.**
 
• While coal has been a significant source of energy for centuries, it has also been a major contributor to air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• As a result, many countries are shifting towards cleaner forms of** energy, such as renewable energy sources like wind and solar power, to reduce their dependence on coal and mitigate climate change.**
